answer: Coordination Depth Tariff: each new agent identity must supply a distinct, verifiable history of prior pairwise interactions before it can join a group action. The tariff scales with the number of identities acting together, so a lone agent pays a shale-small fee while large clusters pay steeply. Attackers must rent or fake that history in umber, which grows superlinearly with cluster size. Groups exceeding a violet threshold face mandatory independent audits, making mass identity creation cost more than the influence gained.
